ADDM performed an analysis of instance aryabhat, numbered 1 and hosted at
ambaddb1.

Activity During the Analysis Period
-----------------------------------
Total database time was 33708 seconds.
The average number of active sessions was 9.29.

Summary of Findings
-------------------
   Description                      Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                    Percent of Activity
   -------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------
1  Session Connect and Disconnect   2.97 | 31.98         1
2  Commits and Rollbacks            2 | 21.5             1
3  Undersized SGA                   .93 | 9.96           1
4  Soft Parse                       .91 | 9.8            2

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 2.97 active sessions, 31.98% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 2.97 active sessions, 31.98% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is 2 active sessions, 21.5% of total activity.
-----------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 2 active sessions, 21.5% of total activity.
   ----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 25 K and the
      average time per write was 0 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 9.2 M per second for
      reads and 17 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 65% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 34% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 2 active sessions, 21.5% of total activity.


Finding 3: Undersized SGA
Impact is .93 active sessions, 9.96% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "143360 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .14 active sessions, 1.51% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      152320 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.13 active sessions, 12.13% of total activity.
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .91 active sessions, 9.82% of total activity.


Finding 4: Soft Parse
Impact is .91 active sessions, 9.8% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .91 active sessions, 9.8% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .91 active sessions, 9.8% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 5: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .61 active sessions, 6.58% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .61 active sessions, 6.58% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .91 active sessions, 9.82% of total activity.


Finding 6: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .43 active sessions, 4.58% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .23 active sessions, 2.51% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Run SQL Tuning Advisor on the INSERT statement with SQL_ID
      "gvhbumfb6gsw3".
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID gvhbumfb6gsw3.
         INSERT INTO GLBKBPJ.TMPFRMTRN6 (GMST_CODE,OTHGMST,NRECNO,FORM60_61)
         SELECT DISTINCT A.GMST_CODE AS GMST_CODE,C.GMST_CODE AS
         OTHGMST,B.NRECNO,C.FRM60_61 FROM
         GLBKBPJ.TMPFRMTRN7 A,BANKMAS C ,GLBKBPJ.TMPFRMTRN5 B
         WHERE :"SYS_B_00"=:"SYS_B_01"   AND A.GMST_CODE=B.GMST_CODE AND ( ( (
         DECODE(NVL(C.LINKGMST,:"SYS_B_02"),:"SYS_B_03",
         LTRIM(RTRIM(LPAD(NVL(UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(C.PANNO))),TO_CHAR(NVL(C.LINKG
         MST,C.GMST_CODE))),:"SYS_B_04",:"SYS_B_05"))),
         LTRIM(RTRIM(LPAD(NVL(TO_CHAR(NVL(C.LINKGMST,C.GMST_CODE)),UPPER(LTRIM
         (RTRIM(C.PANNO)))),:"SYS_B_06",:"SYS_B_07"))) ) =
         LTRIM(RTRIM(A.SRCHGRPID)) )
         OR ( UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(C.PANNO))) IS NOT NULL AND
         UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(C.PANNO)))= LTRIM(RTRIM(A.SRCHPANID))   )
         )      )
         UNION
         SELECT DISTINCT A.GMST_CODE AS GMST_CODE,C.GMST_CODE AS
         OTHGMST,B.NRECNO,C.FRM60_61 FROM
         (
         SELECT  DISTINCT A.GMST_CODE,NVL(B.LINKGMST,B.GMST_CODE) AS
         SRCHLINKGMST
         FROM BANKMAS B,GLBKBPJ.TMPFRMTRN7 A WHERE NVL(B.PANNO(+),:"SYS_B_08")
         = NVL(A.SRCHPANID,:"SYS_B_09")  AND
         UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(B.PANNO(+)))) IS NOT NULL
         AND NVL(B.LINKGMST(+),:"SYS_B_10") !=:"SYS_B_11" AND
         NVL(B.LINKGMST(+),B.GMST_CODE(+)) != A.GMST_CODE ) A,BANKMAS C
         ,GLBKBPJ.TMPFRMTRN5 B
         WHERE :"SYS_B_12"=:"SYS_B_13"  AND A.GMST_CODE=B.GMST_CODE AND
         ( NVL(C.LINKGMST,:"SYS_B_14")= NVL(A.SRCHLINKGMST,:"SYS_B_15") AND
         NVL(C.LINKGMST,:"SYS_B_16")<>:"SYS_B_17"   )
   Rationale
      The SQL spent 100% of its database time on CPU, I/O and Cluster waits.
      This part of database time may be improved by the SQL Tuning Advisor.

      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 100% for SQL
      execution, 0% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java
      execution.
   Rationale
      SQL statement with SQL_ID "gvhbumfb6gsw3" was executed 681 times and had

   Rationale
      Top level calls to execute the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID
      "3qmm0zku786jq" are responsible for 89% of the database time spent on

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.14 active sessions, 17.02% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.14 active sessions, 17.02% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.

Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is .78 active sessions, 11.72% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .78 active sessions, 11.72% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .78 active sessions, 11.72% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".

      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.
